cultural.vision_reason: This is a Thai Buddhist votive amulet depicting Khun Chang, a figure from a Thai folk epic, worn as a personal amulet in presentation packaging — a traditional Thai ritual/devotional object rather than jewelry per se.

physical.title: tablet; amulet
physical.summary: Votive tablet of Khun Chang. Votive sealing or amulet bearing a high-relief depiction of Khun Chang, the anti-hero of Khun Chang Khun Phaen, a popular traditional Thai story. The plump bare-chested figure squats with his right leg curled in front of him and the left upright and bent. The right hand grips his money bag. On the back of the sealing is a magic symbol. The sealing has a rectangular shape with a rounded top and is made of an impressed white substance. It is in a small standard-style presentation box for amulets, plastic with a hinged cover with machine-inscribed floral and other motifs and the name of the figure and the monastery in Thai, and a red velvet-like cushion.
